overall_summary: The channel's clear breakout category is extreme space and exoplanet anomalies, with videos focusing on bizarre cosmic weather (burning ice, ruby rain, coal-dark skies) consistently generating the highest views and engagement. Conversely, abstract psychology facts and repetitive brain-related topics struggle to gain traction, even when re-uploaded.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,007 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (719 views) represent the top tier of performance.
winning_patterns.action: Produce a dedicated series on extreme exoplanet environments, focusing on high-contrast visual concepts (e.g., glass rain, diamond oceans, metal clouds).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' achieved 368 views, outperforming standard space facts.
winning_patterns.action: Use sensory hooks (smell, taste, touch) to explain scientific phenomena in space to make abstract concepts tangible.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flatlined at 5 to 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' only reached 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out text-heavy or abstract psychology facts. If covering biology, pivot to extreme animal survival mechanisms which perform better (e.g., 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter' with 179 views).

next_video.concept: WASP-12b, the egg-shaped planet being actively consumed and stretched by its parent star.
next_video.opening_direction: This planet is shaped like a giant egg because its own star is literally eating it alive.
next_video.twist_direction: In less than 10 million years, it will be completely swallowed, leaving behind nothing but a trail of cosmic dust.
next_video.reason: Aligns with the highly successful exoplanet anomaly trend. The 'egg-shaped' visual and the concept of a planet being 'eaten' provide strong retention hooks.

experiment: Test a 'Space Horror' narrative style using cinematic, AI-generated visuals of cosmic destruction to see if it increases average view duration compared to standard educational slideshows.
